# Provenance NOTICE File

A separate, plain-text `NOTICE` at the repository root whose only job is to draw the line between
**what the author made and what the author borrowed**. Three repositories carry one, and in each the
line is drawn around a different risk.

## The three instances

| Repo | The boundary it draws |
|---|---|
| [[research-methodologies-open-set-recognition]] | own writing, structure, mermaid diagrams and the redrawn figure are MIT; the nine cited papers and the AUROC numbers are not the authors' |
| [[it-applications-in-business-and-commerce]] | the team's code and docs are MIT; TORCS, the SCR protocol and `gym_torcs` are third-party — TORCS is a **runtime prerequisite, explicitly not redistributed**, and the upstream `gym_torcs` licence is preserved verbatim in-tree |
| [[labour-fraud-analysis]] | the loudest of the three: a `SYNTHETIC DATA — READ FIRST` banner declaring every name, identifier and narrative in the repo invented, while the data's *shape* and the analytical techniques are carried over from a real matter |

Three different reasons — academic attribution, licence compliance, and disclosure ethics — reaching
for the same artefact. That convergence is what makes this a pattern rather than three coincidences.

## Evidence

> "It summarises and cites third-party scholarly work, which remains the property"
> — Research Methodologies/NOTICE, 2026-07-11

> "This repository is a PORTFOLIO project built on a REAL, ACTIVE investigation."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/NOTICE, 2026-07-11

## Why a separate file, not a README section

A README is a sales document — it is read for what the project *does*. `NOTICE` is the file you
look in when you need to know what you may reuse and what you must not claim, and putting it at the
root under a conventional name means the answer does not depend on anyone reading the tour. It also
survives the README being rewritten, which in this source set happens often
([[readme-as-guided-tour]] pages are edited in dedicated presentation commits).

The Research Methodologies instance is the strictest: the benchmark table is fenced off in its own
`NOTICE` section, *and* flagged inline under the table in the report, *and* again in the licence
footer. The same fact stated three times in three files is the point — see
[[report-cites-benchmarks-rather-than-reproducing]].

## Relation to the broader habit

This is the file-shaped specialisation of [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]], which covers the
same instinct expressed inline: OpenStax figure citations in [[physics-exam-prep]], "not legal
advice" in [[privacy-policy-template]], "not experiments run for this coursework" in the OSR report.
The inline form is more common; the `NOTICE` form is what appears when the boundary is legal rather
than merely epistemic.

Prefer the inline form for a caveat about a *claim*, and the file for a caveat about *ownership* —
the second needs to be findable without reading the prose.
